entities.name: PMID:27489082
observations: Large-scale cross-sectional study of 45,540 ostensibly healthy Chinese men aged 55–69 years screened at Beijing Shijitan Hospital from 2008–2015.
Used PSA density and PSA mass density to adjust for prostate volume and plasma volume; multivariable regression estimated an 11.3% lower serum PSA with metabolic syndrome.
Authors concluded enlarged prostate partly concealed the actual PSA-lowering effect of metabolic syndrome.

entities.name: Metabolic syndrome
observations: Presence of metabolic syndrome was independently associated with lower serum PSA; increasing numbers of metabolic-syndrome components showed a significant linear association with declining PSA.
Metabolic syndrome was associated with larger prostate volume in the studied population, which partly concealed the PSA-lowering effect before prostate-volume adjustment.

entities.name: Serum PSA
observations: After accounting for prostate volume and plasma volume using PSA density and PSA mass density, PSA was significantly lower in men with metabolic syndrome; adjusted mean serum PSA was estimated to be 11.3% lower.
The study concerns PSA interpretation in men with metabolic syndrome rather than proving a causal biological mechanism.

entities.name: Enlarged prostate
observations: Larger prostate volume among men with metabolic syndrome partly concealed the underlying PSA-lowering association; adjustment increased the estimated difference between metabolic-syndrome groups.
